by: tools/sanborn/complete/merge_reads.py: two independent reads, a pick only where they agree within 60 px

bends.note: angle point, turns from south-east to south-south-east
angle point, turns back to south-east; south-west side cut by plate edge, centre approximate

ends.note: interrupted by the railroad; continues north-west of the tracks from about (4225, 915) to the plate edge
ends at Railroad Avenue and the railroad

notes: Strip is mostly factories, rail sidings and the Mill Creek. The 40 ft avenue running north-west from Spring Grove Avenue at (4828,1795) has only 'AVE.' printed inside the strip; the name CHICKERING is printed on its continuation north-west of the railroad (about x 3800-3950, y 250-450), so it is recorded as Chickering Avenue. Spring Grove Avenue's name is not printed inside the strip (identified by its 100 ft width and house numbers 4878-5106). Kessler: only 'KESSLER' read, suffix assumed Avenue. Mitchell Avenue crosses the Mill Creek near (4550,5130) (bridge, not a crossing); the street 'AVENUE' label is printed east of the strip. Hope Street name printed at about (3960,3230); its width figure at the Durham end is unclear (40, 50 or 60), drawn about 50 ft. Durham Avenue is printed 40 but drawn about 46 ft wide. | Spring Grove Avenue name is not printed inside the strip (identified by its 100 ft width, car tracks and 48xx-51xx house numbers); Mitchell Avenue name is printed west of the strip near x 3500, y 4250; Kessler's suffix is not printed in the strip, Avenue assumed. Durham Avenue and Railroad Avenue meet as an L corner; Ammen Avenue and Railroad Avenue likewise (at the strip's left margin). Mitchell Avenue's south-west side is cut by the plate edge at Kessler, so that centre is less certain (about 20 px). The Erie Canal strip (lettered ERIE CANAL, 75 ft) crossing Mitchell near 5450,5850 is not a street. No other crossings in the strip: the middle is rail yards, factories and the Mill Creek.
